en.title: Formal and informal register
en.summary: Register is the level of formality of language.

paragraphs: Register is the level of formality that a speaker or writer chooses for a situation. English has a range from very formal (legal documents, official letters) through neutral to informal (conversation with friends) and slang. Using the wrong register can sound rude, cold or childish.

items: **I would be grateful if you could...** (formal)

paragraphs: Consider who you are speaking to, what the situation is and what the medium is. A letter of application, a report and a speech are formal; a text message to a friend is informal; an e-mail to a colleague is neutral.

paragraphs: Slang and colloquial words (mate, cool, kid, quid) are very informal and belong to particular groups or regions. They change quickly. Avoid them in writing or in formal situations unless you know the context well.

items: Wrong: **Dear Mr Smith, Hi! Wanna meet?** Mixed registers.
Wrong: **Yours faithfully, Mr Smith** (when you know the name) Right: **Yours sincerely**
Wrong: **I request you to give me information at your earliest convenience hereby.** (too heavy) Right: **Could you send me the information, please?**

ro.title: Registrul formal și informal
ro.summary: Registrul arată nivelul de politețe folosit când vorbim sau scriem în diferite situații sociale.

paragraphs: Registrul reprezintă modul în care adaptăm vorbirea la situație. Folosim registrul informal cu prietenii și cu familia. Folosim registrul formal cu persoane necunoscute sau la birou.

În limba română, registrul formal folosește pronume de politețe precum „dumneavoastră”. Verbul primește atunci forma de plural pentru a arăta respect. În registrul informal, vorbim direct și folosim pronumele „tu”.
